title: Handoff Horizon: Week-of Mar 15-19, 2027 — Latency Forensics & SLO Notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary

This is the on-call handoff / weekly synthesis focused on the mid-week latency spike we chased on Mar 17, plus SLO drift observed in the embeddings path. Meant as the single source for next-step owners, timeline, and quick mitigations for the follow-on rotation. Keep it short for the next oncall to pick up.

Topline takeaways
- Incident on 2027-03-17 14:08 UTC caused 95th- and 99th-percentile token-latency regressions for hosted-api chat endpoints (chat.generate). Peak degradation lasted ~18 minutes.
- Primary user-facing symptoms: streaming stalls and delayed first-byte for long-context requests (>2k tokens).
- Initial root hypothesis (fast): the new kernel selection policy in runtime v2.8.1 incorrectly preferred an int8 path for a small subset of llama-family variants at sequence shapes we rarely exercise. This produced memory thrash on a subset of GPU pools.
- Secondary hypothesis (contributing): autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration allowed a capacity dip while several large customers burst simultaneously.
- SLO impact: chat.generate availability SLO (99.5 p99 threshold) breached for 16 minutes; we recorded a 0.8 percentage point excursion. Embeddings ingest pipeline showed 10–15% higher P95 latencies during the same window.

Incident timeline (concise, for handoff)
- 2027-03-17 14:06 UTC — first alerts: p99 latency channel (pager) fires. Paging routed to oncall.
- 14:08 UTC — oncall triage: alerted to streaming stalls; traffic backpressure observed on the dispatcher.
- 14:12 UTC — fallback route enabled: traffic to older runtime pool (v2.7.x) for the affected models via routing policy; initial latency improved.
- 14:20 UTC — deeper investigation: patterns show affected requests are long-context, quantized model variants, and GPUs in eu-west-1 pool type gtx-q4b.
- 14:28 UTC — rolling patch: coordinator changed kernel-selection whitelist to force int4 path for the affected variants; memory churn reduced.
- 14:34 UTC — autoscaler bounce observed: two nodes in eu-west-1 drained mid-incident while burst traffic arrived, contributing to tail-latency.
- 14:40 UTC — full mitigation: both kernel-selection rollback and temporary reserve capacity applied. Latency returned to baseline by ~14:46 UTC.
- 14:50 UTC — incident declared resolved; follow-ups assigned.

Immediate mitigations taken during the page
- Switched routing to v2.7.x pools for affected model ids (manual override). Owner: oncall (Samir).
- Forced kernel-selection to the legacy int4 path for the failing model family. Owner: runtime team (Jordan).
- Increased temporary reserved capacity in eu-west-1 (burst reserve +50%). Owner: infra (Marta).
- Short-term alert tuning to capture memory-thrash signatures (new metric alert). Owner: observability (Priya).

Collected evidence and diagnostics (where to look)
- Grafana dashboards: /dashboards/ops/latency/chat.generate (timestamps 2027-03-17 13:55–15:00 UTC).
- Traces: X-Trace IDs attached to JIRA SRE-4812 (see linked_artifacts).
- Kernel-selection logs: runtime-coordinator logs (pod runtime-coordinator-eu-west-1) — grep for kernel_hint and quant_mode.
- Autoscaler events: infra-autoscaler history (eu-west-1, group: q4b-pool).
- Heap and GPU-utilization snapshots: stored in s3://redwood-dumps/forensics/2027-03-17-q4b/

Root cause analysis (working hypothesis)
- Primary cause: a regression in runtime v2.8.1 where the kernel-selection heuristic prioritized an int8 execution path for sequence shapes that result from prefix/cached KV sizes in long-context requests for quantized models. The int8 codepath has a latent memory fragmentation case on our current cudnn/cuda configuration that manifests under sustained burst.
- Contributing cause: autoscaler cooldown was 8m (too long) and a scheduled capacity maintenance (rolling patch) overlapped with customer bursts. This produced transient under-provisioning.
- Why we missed it in staging: our synthetic long-context stress tests do not fully exercise the v2.8.1 int8 branch with realistic cache warmups — mismatch between synthetic traffic and production prefix patterns.

Action items (owner / ETA / status)
- Action: backport kernel-selection whitelist fix (force int4 for sensitive model variants) to v2.8.1 and push hotfix v2.8.2. Owner: Jordan. ETA: 2027-03-21. Status: in_progress.
- Action: add targeted long-context KV-warmup test to staged CI (simulate >2k token prefix shapes). Owner: runtime QA (Priya). ETA: 2027-03-26. Status: todo.
- Action: shorten autoscaler cooldown for critical gpu pools from 8m -> 2m and create an exception during planned capacity maintenance windows. Owner: infra (Marta). ETA: 2027-03-23. Status: todo.
- Action: create post-incident canary that exercises quantized int8 branch under load, run daily for 2 weeks. Owner: applied-ml (Alex). ETA: 2027-03-24. Status: todo.
- Action: update runbook 'quantized-kernel-fallback' with explicit rollback/run-retry steps and include new diagnostic grep patterns. Owner: eng-docs (Samir). ETA: 2027-03-22. Status: in_progress.

SLO snapshot and notes
- Chat.generate (hosted-api): target p99 < 450ms (SLO 99.5%). On 2027-03-17 around the incident window we observed p99 ~1.8s for ~16m. The SLO breach is recorded under SRE-4827.
- Embeddings.ingest pipeline: p95 normally ~120ms; during the incident p95 rose to ~200ms for ~20m. No SLO breach configured (we should consider adding SLO for this path).
- Proposal: add a secondary SLO for embeddings ingest p95 with 30d review — raise as RFC. Owner: product-observability.

Handoff notes for next oncall (practical checklist)
- Check whether hotfix v2.8.2 is deployed; if not, escalate to Jordan and push canary to one region first.
- Confirm temporary reserved capacity in eu-west-1 remains until 2027-03-22; do not scale down during maintenance windows for that pool.
- Watch for recurring memory-thrash alerts: new metric alert name "runtime.kernel.memory-thrash.euw" in practical-alerts channel.
- If similar stalls occur again, immediately disable kernel-selection heuristic at coordinator level and route traffic to v2.7.x pools. That should restore tail latency quickly.
- Add note to the handoff channel with a short summary and a link to this doc so weekends oncall have context.

Meeting notes: post-incident review (Mar 18 review session)
- Attendees: Alex (SRE lead), Jordan (runtime), Priya (QA), Marta (infra), Samir (docs), product-obs rep.
- Key decision: prioritize runtime hotfix and CI test changes. We agreed to a fast-tracked v2.8.2 with the whitelist change + telemetry.
- Follow-up: infra will audit all critical pools for overlapping maintenance windows; any overlaps with major customer bursts should be blocked unless explicit risk sign-off is recorded.

Open questions / unknowns
- How many model variants actually hit the int8 branch in production under regular traffic? Need telemetry granularity.
- Why autoplace/allocator chose two specific nodes to drain mid-incident — was there an internal maintenance signal or unrelated pod eviction?
- Impact to Dedicated customers — did any dedicated pool experience similar tail events? We have a small signal but need to correlate with customer support tickets.

Notes to self (informal, to be helpful to next rotation)
- When you chase streaming stalls, first check: dispatcher backpressure -> kernel-selection logs -> gpu memory fragmentation patterns -> autoscaler activity. Saves ~10min over random chasing.
- Use the "long-context-kernel-trace" query in traces playground; it groups traces by KV-warmup history.
- Slack threads: #sre-oncall and #runtime-kernels both contain the key snippets; grep for "mar17-int8" in the runtime thread.

Appendix: quick references and commands
- Check coordinator logs: kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/runtime-coordinator-eu-west-1 --since=3h | grep "kernel_hint"
- Autoscaler history: aws s3 cp s3://infra-metrics/autoscaler-history/eu-west-1/q4b-pool.json -
- Memory dump locations: s3://redwood-dumps/forensics/2027-03-17-q4b/
- JIRA: SRE-4812 (incident ticket), SRE-4827 (postmortem tracking)

If you're picking this up: leave a short note in the handoff channel summarizing what you did before you finish your shift. Helps the follow-up rotation.

-- Alex (SRE Lead)
